## Key Concepts
- Per-namespace Deployment

## Code Example

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: namespace-scanner
  namespace: <namespace>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: namespace-scanner
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: namespace-scanner
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: install-tools
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-progress curl jq"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical CKAD skills: wiring ConfigMaps and Secrets, configuring InitContainers, implementing TLS sidecars, setting up readiness/liveness probes, and crafting a NetworkPolicy with conditional egress.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMap-driven feature flags
- Secrets for credential management
- InitContainers for tooling installation
- TLS sidecars for secure communication
- Readiness and liveness probe configuration
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: feature-config
data:
  ENABLE_API: "true"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: api-creds
type: Opaque
data:
  token: <base64-encoded-token>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: app-namespace
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: egress-policy
  namespace: app-namespace
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: internal-api
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 8080
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-app
  namespace: app-namespace
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: my-app
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: installer
          image: curlimages/curl:latest
          command: ['sh', '-c', 'echo Initialized']
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: my-app:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          env:
            - name: ENABLE_API
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: feature-config
                  key: ENABLE_API
            - name: API_TOKEN
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: api-creds
                  key: token
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /status
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /status
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
        - name: tls-sidecar
          image: nginx:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 443
```

## Trade-offs
- **NetworkPolicy complexity**: The policy above allows egress only to the internal-api pod. A more permissive approach might allow DNS resolution but restrict target services.
- **InitContainer overhead**: Installing curl in every pod increases startup time and image size. Consider baking tools into the base image if startup latency is critical.
- **Sidecar maintenance**: A TLS sidecar adds complexity and resource overhead. For simple use cases, TLS could be handled within the application container directly.
- **Secret security**: Storing credentials in a Secret is fine for basic scenarios, but consider external secrets operators or vault integration for production environments requiring rotation.
- **Probe configuration**: Aggressive probe settings can cause unnecessary restarts; conservative settings may delay failure detection. Tune based on application startup time.

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests hands-on CKAD skills: in-cluster configuration, API access, and multi-resource coordination. It evaluates how the candidate wires ConfigMaps, Secrets, and PVCs into a Deployment, and how they enforce traffic restrictions with a NetworkPolicy.

## Key Concepts

- Namespace-scoped Deployment and RBAC permissions
- ConfigMap-based thresholds and Secret-based credentials
- API access to Namespace ResourceQuota metrics
- InitContainer usage for tools like curl/jq
- Logs persisted to a PVC mounted at /logs
- Readiness and liveness probes
- Namespace NetworkPolicy to restrict egress to the central endpoint

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: alert-config
data:
  cpu-threshold: "80"
  memory-threshold: "85"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: alert-credentials
data:
  api-key: <base64-encoded-key>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: log-storage
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: resource-watcher
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: resource-watcher
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: resource-watcher
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: installer
          image: busybox
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |-
                wget -q https://github.com/stedolan/jq/releases/download/jq-1.6/jq-linux64 -O /usr/local/bin/jq
                chmod +x /usr/local/bin/jq
                apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /usr/local/bin
      containers:
        - name: watcher
          image: your-watcher-image:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
              name: http
          env:
            - name: CENTRAL_ENDPOINT
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: alert-credentials
                  key: api-key
          volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
            - name: config
              mountPath: /config
              readOnly: true
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
          resources:
            requests:
              memory: "64Mi"
              cpu: "50m"
            limits:
              memory: "128Mi"
              cpu: "100m"
      volumes:
        - name: logs
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: log-storage
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: alert-config
        - name: tools
          emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: egress-restriction
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: resource-watcher
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              name: central-monitoring
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 443
```

## Trade-offs

1. **Polling vs. Watch API**: Polling ResourceQuota is simpler but adds latency; the Watch API is more efficient but requires handling event streams.
2. **Sidecar vs. Main Container**: A sidecar could handle logging while the main container focuses on monitoring—improving separation of concerns.
3. **Centralized vs. Per-Namespace**: Deploying per-namespace increases resource usage but provides isolation and reduces blast radius.
4. **PVC for Logs**: Using a PVC adds persistence but requires storage provisioning; consider sidecar streaming to stdout for easier management.
5. **InitContainer Overhead**: Downloading tools on every pod start slows startup; a custom image with tools pre-installed would be faster.

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates CKAD competencies in CronJob scheduling, InitContainers for tooling bootstrap, PVC-mounted database operations, health probes, lifecycle hooks, and rollback strategies.

## Key Concepts
- **CronJob**: Scheduled jobs using cron syntax (0 2 * * * for daily at 02:00)
- **InitContainer**: Bootstrap tool installation (sqlite3) before main container runs
- **SQLite Operations**: DELETE with WHERE clause for date filtering, VACUUM for storage reclamation
- **Probes**: readinessProbe and livenessProbe on /healthz endpoint
- **Lifecycle Hooks**: preStop sleep for graceful shutdown
- **PodDisruptionBudget**: minAvailable: 1 ensures availability during disruptions

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: log-pruner
  namespace: ckad-practices
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app: log-pruner
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          initContainers:
          - name: installer
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache sqlite"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: db
              mountPath: /data
          containers:
          - name: pruner
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "sqlite3 /data/logs.db 'DELETE FROM logs WHERE created_at < date(\"now\", \"-30 days\"); VACUUM;'; curl -X POST -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{\"deleted\":\"$(date)\"}' http://ops-portal:8080/api/v1/prune-summary"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: db
              mountPath: /data
            resources:
              requests:
                memory: "64Mi"
                cpu: "100m"
              limits:
                memory: "128Mi"
                cpu: "500m"
            readinessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /healthz
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /healthz
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 15
              periodSeconds: 20
            lifecycle:
              preStop:
                exec:
                  command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 5"]
          volumes:
          - name: db
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-pvc
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: log-pruner-pdb
  namespace: ckad-practices
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: log-pruner
```

## Rollback Strategy
Maintain version-controlled YAML manifests in a Git repository. On failure, execute:
```bash
kubectl apply -f log-pruner.yaml --record
kubectl rollout undo cronjob/log-pruner
```
Alternatively, use a GitOps tool like ArgoCD or Flux for automated rollbacks.

## Why This Is Asked
Security hardening of container runtimes and correctness of patching deployments are critical in real-world CKAD tasks.

## Key Concepts
- SecurityContext: runAsNonRoot, runAsUser, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities drop
- Probes: readiness and liveness on /healthz

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: portal
  namespace: secure-app
spec:
  replicas: 2
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 0
      maxSurge: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: portal
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: portal
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:1.25

          httpGet:
            path: /healthz

          periodSeconds: 10
          timeoutSeconds: 2
        livenessProbe:

            path: /healthz

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of InitContainer lifecycle, idempotent seeding patterns, and persistent cache management across pod restarts.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainers and startup ordering
- ConfigMap-based seed script injection
- PVC-backed shared cache for idempotence
- Marker file pattern for preventing re-seeding
- Readiness and liveness probe configuration

## Code Example
```yaml
# Seed script ConfigMap
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: seed-scripts
data:
  seed.sh: |
    #!/bin/sh
    set -e
    if [ ! -f /cache/.seeded ]; then
      # Execute seeding logic here
      touch /cache/.seeded
    fi
---
# Deployment with InitContainer
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-server
  namespace: ckad
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: seed-cache
        image: busybox:1.35
        command: ['/bin/sh', '/scripts/seed.sh']
        volumeMounts:
        - name: seed-scripts
          mountPath: /scripts
        - name: cache-volume
          mountPath: /cache
      containers:
      - name: api-server
        image: api-server:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: cache-volume
          mountPath: /cache
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
      - name: seed-scripts
        configMap:
          name: seed-scripts
      - name: cache-volume
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: cache-pvc
```

3. **Monitoring**: Check InitContainer logs, verify probe status, and confirm cache persistence across pod restarts
